description: ChainDrop (Mini Shai-Hulud) npm worm detection data (G-1482 wave-spec engine, TRAV-02) — the same IOC set scripts/scan-chaindrop-aug2026.sh hardcodes in bash arrays and manifests/chaindrop-poisoned-versions.json documents, now expressed as one versioned, validated spec so the traversal engine's NEXT live wave is 'a spec plus tests', not a fifth standalone scanner. Poisoned releases carry VALID GitHub-Actions/SLSA provenance, so `npm audit signatures` PASSES them — detection must be IOC-based. FAIL only on a version listed in poisonedVersions; family presence at a pre-attack version is NOT an IOC (these are ubiquitous eslint transitive deps). See docs/supply-chain-defense.md and manifests/chaindrop-poisoned-versions.json (parity-tested against this file, never generated-from — D-10).

variantPattern.note: The stage-2 harvester also ships under generated variant names (Math_<guid>.js). FAIL when the file carries a knownBadHashes match or is >= sizeThresholdBytes (the real stage-2 is ~727KB); otherwise WARN so a renamed variant surfaces instead of silently passing. Exact names already covered by fileMarkers.fail are excluded here to avoid a double report (script:206-227).

knownBadHashes.description: Math_Symbol.js / math_init.js — stage-2 Bun-bundled harvester. This is the reason the targeted hash-candidate tier is NOT capped at the 256k bulk-content-scan size (D-24): the real payload is 727,680 bytes, well over that cap, and hashing it with the bulk cap would silently stop detecting the actual ChainDrop stage-2 payload.
setup.mjs — later-wave loader (exits non-zero on error)

installMarker.note: D-25: bash section 2 (script:277-289) scans package.json via `grep -rlE` with NO directory prune at all — not even PRUNE_COMMON applies. This check must run inside node_modules (and every other directory) too, or it silently loses coverage the bash scanner has today.

claudeSettings.note: Glob patterns matched during the walk (agent-config class), covering any project's .claude/settings.json — in addition to the two static $HOME paths listed in staticPaths (script:399/402-423, HOOK_SUS_RE). commandPattern is POSIX ERE for bash `grep -E` (scripts/scan-chaindrop-aug2026.sh:512, the two static-path check); jsCommandPattern is the SAME IOC set with `[[:space:]]` rewritten to `\s` for JS `new RegExp()` (lib/traverse/engine.js), which does not understand POSIX bracket classes — `[[:space:]]` in a JS RegExp is a literal character class of `[`,`:`,`s`,`p`,`a`,`c`,`e`,`]`, not whitespace (G-1482 merge-blocking fix, 2026-08-10). Keep both patterns' non-whitespace IOC terms identical; only the whitespace-class spelling differs.

vscodeTasks.note: failPattern is POSIX ERE and, unlike claudeSettings.commandPattern, has no bash consumer today — only lib/traverse/engine.js reads persistence.vscodeTasks fields, so this field's POSIX `[[:space:]]` was a silent no-op miss from day one, not a regression against a working bash check. jsFailPattern is the same IOC set with `[[:space:]]` -> `\s` for JS `new RegExp()` (G-1482 merge-blocking fix, 2026-08-10). triggerPattern above contains no POSIX bracket class and needs no js* counterpart.

all-files.note: Bash sections 1a/1a2/1b/5 (filename markers, variant pattern, setup.mjs triage, known-bad-hash candidates) — PRUNE_COMMON only, node_modules IS walked.

no-prune.note: Bash section 2 (installMarker/preinstall grep) — no directory prune at all, per D-25. Consumes: installMarker.

lockfiles.note: Bash section 3a — lockfile scan, PRUNE_COMMON + node_modules excluded. Consumes: lockfiles + poisonedVersions.

family-packages.note: Bash section 3b — deliberately walks INTO node_modules to find installed compromised-family package.json files; only worktrees are pruned, PRUNE_COMMON does not apply. Consumes: compromisedFamily + poisonedVersions.

agent-config.note: Bash sections 4a/4b — .claude/settings*.json + .vscode/tasks.json scans, PRUNE_COMMON + node_modules excluded. Consumes: persistence.

bulk-content.note: Bash section 6b — marker-string content scan. PRUNE_COMMON + node_modules + .cache excluded, extension/name allowlist (script:491-493), size cap = bounds.bulkReadCapBytes. Consumes: markerStrings.

bounds.note: `find -size -256k` and `-size -1024k` are block-rounded bounds, so 262144 and 1048576 are chosen as the smallest values that are a SUPERSET of what bash reads today — the engine may read slightly more than the old scanner did, never less, because losing coverage is the one unacceptable outcome of this refactor.
